summary: Iteration-7 review: wallet-deposit Telegram-approval flow + customizable bot payment-info + admin chat-id list + clickable Receipt page + receipt email. All 18 backend pytest cases pass and all 7 frontend UI flows verified on the live preview URL. ONE BUG FOUND AND FIXED in /app/backend/server.py: _approve_deposit_internal and _reject_deposit_internal returned the raw Mongo deposit doc (with ObjectId _id) inside the response, causing /api/admin/wallet/deposits/{id}/approve and /reject to return 500 'ValueError: ObjectId is not iterable' instead of 200. Wrapped the deposit dicts with _clean() before returning. After the fix, full approve→credit→receipt-email→WTX-* row→/me/wallet/transactions/{txn_id} round-trip works end-to-end.

action_items: Validate the _clean() fix to the deposit approval/reject internals (added by testing agent) — see updated_files below. Without this fix, the entire admin wallet approve/reject endpoints returned 500.
critical_code_review_comments: [FIXED] _approve_deposit_internal and _reject_deposit_internal returned the raw Mongo deposit doc which contained ObjectId `_id`, causing FastAPI's jsonable_encoder to throw 'ObjectId is not iterable' → HTTP 500. Fixed in this iteration by wrapping `dep` in `_clean(dep)` in the four return statements (lines 797, 799, 847, 857, 875). The same defensive _clean() was already used by every other wallet endpoint — these helpers were inconsistent. Strongly recommend adding a pytest asserting 'no _id field in any /api/admin/wallet/deposits/* response body' as a regression guard.

POST /api/admin/wallet/deposits/{id}/reject uses `reason` as a QUERY parameter (?reason=...), which forces frontends to URL-encode the string and limits length. Consider moving it into a JSON body for consistency with the rest of the admin API.

POST /api/me/wallet/deposit has WalletDepositRequestIn.method constrained to '^(manual|crypto)$' but the frontend payment_info UI exposes UPI everywhere; suggest renaming 'manual' → 'upi' OR documenting that UPI deposits are submitted under method='manual'. The current pattern blocked our first test attempt (we sent 'upi' and got a 422).

Race condition risk: _approve_deposit_internal reads dep, then calls _wallet_txn, then $sets status='approved' — two concurrent approve calls on the same deposit_id can both pass the status check and double-credit. Mitigate with an atomic findOneAndUpdate({id, status:'pending'}, {$set:{status:'approved'}}) before crediting.

send_wallet_receipt_email is fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task; if SMTP is down the user still gets the success response but no receipt email — consider logging the failure so admins can re-send.
server.py is now 4414 lines (was 4091 last iteration). Continues to grow — please split into modules (wallet.py, telegram_bot.py, admin.py).
Cross-user receipt access correctly returns 404 (not 403) — good, prevents user_id enumeration.

rca_of_the_issue: BUG: POST /api/admin/wallet/deposits/{id}/approve and /reject returned HTTP 500. ROOT CAUSE: the internal helpers _approve_deposit_internal / _reject_deposit_internal returned the raw Mongo doc as part of {'ok':True,'deposit':{**dep,...}}; the doc carried Mongo's ObjectId-typed `_id` field which FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ('ObjectId is not iterable'). REPRO: create any deposit then POST /approve → 500. FIX: wrap `dep` with the existing `_clean()` helper (which strips `_id`) in the four return paths (success approve, success reject, 'already approved/rejected' branches in approve, and 'already rejected' branch in reject). VERIFICATION: full 18-test pytest suite now green; end-to-end UI receipt flow now reaches the printable Receipt page with all fields populated.
